newsitem.title: FRANCE: Convicted Carlos again probed for killings.
newsitem.headline: Convicted Carlos again probed for killings.

text.p: Guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal", facing several murder probes in France, is to be questioned on Friday about the only killings for which he has already been convicted, justice sources said on Thursday.
They said Carlos will face France's top anti-terrorist investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere over the Paris killings of two French secret agents and their Lebanese informer in 1975.

The three men and a counter-intelligence chief, all unarmed, had called at a Left Bank flat in Paris. The man who opened the door shot them after a brief discussion and fled. Only the counter-intelligence chief survived.
Carlos, whose real name is Carlos Ilich Ramirez, was found guilty of the killings and sentenced in absentia in 1992 to life in jail.
Under French law he is entitled to a retrial since he did not attend the hearings.

Carlos, spirited away from Sudan in 1994 and now held in a Paris prison, disputes experts' reports that his fingerprints were found at the Paris flat and that the type of pistol used indicates he was the killer, the sources said.
He also denies the authenticity of an interview published in 1979 by the Lebanese daily al-Watan al-Arabi in which he said he had killed the three men.
Carlos says he did not give the interview and it was part of a plot against him by the secret services of an unnamed Middle East country.
The sources said Bruguiere would question Carlos in three sessions this month.
The magistrate is already investigating Carlos over five bomb attacks in France in the 1980s -- two in Paris, two against trains and one in Marseille.

French police accuse Carlos of killing 83 people in a series of attacks in Europe and the Middle East. The boldest attack with which he was linked was the kidnapping of 11 OPEC oil ministers in Vienna in 1975.
